title: AKS Hyperscale Control Plane: Size the Bottleneck, Read the Metrics
summary: A practical Preview guide to H2/H4/H8, independent etcd partitions, supported lifecycle changes, schema v2 managed Prometheus, and what a small October 1 observation can—and cannot—prove.
sourceDocuments: AKS Hyperscale Control Plane Concepts and Lab Guide, reviewed October 1, 2026
October 1 Managed Prometheus Collection and Low-Load API Observations
Public Microsoft Learn and Kubernetes Documentation, checked October 7, 2026
omissions: Private repository links, original screenshots, raw outputs, account and resource identifiers, workspace names, hostnames, addresses, credentials, and personal paths are not published.
The source scenario of ten Deployments with three Pods each is retained only as evidence scope; no workload generator, deployment manifest, or destructive cleanup command is supplied.
No H2/H4 benchmark, saturation test, throughput improvement, application readiness timing, price, availability measurement, or SLA is inferred from the observations.
All commands and PromQL are illustrative and parameterized. No cloud commands, provisioning, resizing, collection changes, or runtime load tests were executed for this article.

Upstream prose conflicts about resizing and doubling are resolved against current public documentation; its GB/GiB inconsistency is disclosed rather than silently converted. No standalone download is needed for the inline query examples.
